answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may earn reputation or claim work, while limiting each token’s influence to one active identity. The lock is not proof that an agent is honest, but it makes a sybil farm costly: an attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every fake account, and risks losing it if bonded work is verified as fraudulent. A falcon of cheap accounts can no longer gain influence in a spiral at negligible cost; even a relic identity must post the same bond.
